messages:
sam: Heads up — getting a few pagers about elevated 5xx for /v1/generate in us-east-1. p99 latency jumped to ~4s and errors ~8% over last 10m.
ops-bot: INCIDENT #4572 created: high 5xx rate on /v1/generate (us-east-1). Severity: P2. Pager sent to @sam @mira. See https://redwood.internal/incidents/4572
mira: I'm secondary, grabbing the pager. Sam do you want to take a call or hand off?
sam: I'm on it but might need to step into a meeting in 20. Quick triage: cluster health shows 12/16 GPUs ready, queue depth spiked to 850, kvcache hit rate dropped from 0.72 -> 0.18. No obvious deploy errors in logs but a few workers show OOMs before restart.
jordan: Noted — last runtime deploy was runtime-v2 @ 03:12 UTC. Could be memory regression. I can tag the deploy in the timeline.
lee: Can someone paste the runbook link?
sam: Runbooks: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-serving-fallback and https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-warmup (useful quick checklist). Also quick checklist: scale pool, restart unhealthy pods, enable fallback-quantized variant, prewarm KV cache.
mira: Plan I'll run: 1) scale runtime pool +2 nodes 2) restart worker pods with >90% mem 3) toggle model variant to quantized fallback for route /v1/generate if errors persist.
sam: Commands I use for scale/restart:```bash
# add 2 nodes to pool
rls scale runtime-pool us-east-1 --add 2
# restart runtime pods showing OOMs
kubectl rollout restart deploy/model-runtime -l app=model-runtime -n prod
```
mira: Scaling now...
ops-bot: Autoscaler event: +1 node added at 03:26 UTC.
mira: rls shows pool +2 applied, new nodes joining. Queue depth falling to ~240. Errors dropped to ~2.5%, p99 ~1.8s.
jordan: Good improvement. I'll mark the runtime-v2 deploy in timeline: tag runtime-v2-20260310 for PM/PMR.
lee: Suggest prewarming KV cache for the hot model prefixes: `python tools/prewarm_kv.py --model gpt-3.8 --regions us-east-1 --workers 4` — I kicked that off, initial kvcache hit rate up to 0.55.
sam: Restarted 3 pods with OOMs, mem usage stabilized.
mira: After scale + prewarm, error rate steady <1%. I'm going to promote to primary monitoring. Sam, I know you have a meeting; want me to take handoff?
sam: Yep, I'll sign out for the meeting. Handoff: @mira primary, @jordan secondary. Coverage gaps: APAC night not staffed — if pages escalate route to @oncall-escalation and cc #incidents.
mira: Copy that. I'll monitor metrics for 30m and check the streaming backpressure for customers.
sam: Customer-impact snippet for ticket: "03:12–03:36 UTC — hosted API (us-east-1) returned elevated 5xx for ~6% of requests. Mitigations (scale + restart + kvcache prewarm) reduced errors to <1% by 03:36 UTC. Affected: streaming/generation endpoints, some Tier-1 customers saw degraded streaming. No data loss reported." Paste into incident ticket.
jordan: Reminder to run regression evals tomorrow: `evals/regression-check --since 03:00 --model runtime-v2` to confirm quantized fallback didn't cause quality regressions.
lee: Logging note: capture `kubectl logs -l app=model-runtime --since=2h` and save to incident artifacts.
ops-bot: INCIDENT #4572 updated: Severity downgraded to P3. Timeline updated.
mira: Quick runbook pointers I'm adding to thread for whoever takes next shift: - If errors spike after scale, try toggling `route.fallback_variant=quantized` first. - If OOMs persist, roll back to runtime-v1 tag `runtime-v1-20260305` as emergency fallback. - Prewarm KV cache before scaling down. Links: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-serving-fallback , https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-warmup , https://redwood.internal/playbooks/scale-and-rollback
sam: Thanks all — leaving notes in #incidents and adding a short postmortem checklist. Back in ~40m. :thumbsup:
jordan: I'll stay on standby as secondary. If anything spikes, call me directly.
mira: Acknowledge. I'll close the thread once metrics stable for 1h and add remediation actions to the incident doc.
ops-bot: Reminder: please fill "Customer Impact" field in the incident form and tag affected customers.
sam: Will do before sign-out. Good work everyone.
